ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (last amended 2023), Articles 5, 5-2 and 5-3; Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information; Act on Regulation and Punishment of Concealment of Criminal Proceeds; Commercial Act, Articles 288 through 317; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Beneficial ownership data is not publicly searchable; financial institutions must collect and file UBO information with the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit under lawful request.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Corporate Registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Office of the competent District Court under the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original registry certificate: obtain a single Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for Hague Apostille Convention member states; for non-member states, obtain MOFA consular legalization and the destination state embassy or consulate in Seoul. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive routes and are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Current Corporate Registration and Registered Particulars)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Office of the competent District Court under the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original registry certificate: obtain a direct Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for Hague Convention states; for non-convention states, use MOFA consular legalization and the destination mission in Seoul. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives and are never applied in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing local counsel to complete incorporation and AML representations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Initial incorporators and subscribers acting by resolution, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the signed resolution and power of attorney at a Korean notary public; for Hague Apostille states, have the notarized document apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. For non-member states, submit the notarized document to MOFA consular legalization and then to the destination state diplomatic mission in Seoul. The two paths are exclusive and must never be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Articles of Incorporation) executed by the incorporators
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators of the company, certified by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the executed articles at a Korean notary public; then apply to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for an Apostille when the destination is a Hague Convention member state. For a non-Hague destination, use MOFA consular legalization followed by the destination embassy/consulate in Seoul. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and are never sequenced together.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming account opening, source of funds and expected grant distribution activity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Have the bank officer's signature and corporate seal notarized by a Korean notary public; for Hague Apostille states, obtain an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. For non-member states, obtain MOFA consular legalization and the destination state embassy or consulate in Seoul. These alternative authentication routes are never chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Perform layered screening of all incorporators, directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, officers, and grant counterparties against the United States OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit terrorist finance designation list, and domestic judgment and wanted-person databases. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any politically exposed person, immediate family member, or close associate; beneficial ownership must be pierced through corporate registries, shareholder ledgers, and nominee declarations. The AML file must include source of funds evidence, bank wire provenance, intended grant destinations, and any FATF high-risk jurisdiction nexus.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry Office (I-Registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered trade name must be written in Hangul script, and the legal-form suffix must appear at the end as the transliterated term 'Chusik Hoesa'. For a foreign founder's non-Hangul name, a statutory phonetic Hangul transliteration is registered; the English spelling on the certificate is ancillary. Four-tier naming control applies: (1) local script is mandatory for the registered name; (2) the legal-form suffix is mandatory; (3) the name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to any existing trade name in the same registry jurisdiction and business category; and (4) no prohibited or sensitive token may be used without prior ministerial approval.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must demand a written refusal from the district court registry specifying the statutory ground. A formal objection may then be filed under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act with the competent district court registry within the statutory appeal period, ordinarily one month. The appeal must include a revised name comparison table, a legal opinion distinguishing the rejected name from existing registered names, and any ministerial approval obtained for a sensitive token. If the court rejects the objection, the applicant should refile with a more distinctive Hangul transliteration name before applying to the appellate registry division.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office and commercial mailbox solutions are generally rejected by the National Tax Service, the district registry, and licensed banks for a charitable endowment entity operating under ISIC 6430. Korean banks apply the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and require physical inspection of office premises; the Act on Regulation of Fundraising and Use of Donations requires actual administrative assets, records, staff, and board access at the registered address. A virtual office may be accepted only if the arrangement includes a staffed physical reception, dedicated workspace, on-premises or immediately available documentation, unrestricted auditor access, and written pre-approval from the tax office and the relevant bank.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: physical lease, utilities, signboard matching the registered name, company seal, certificate of corporate registration, payroll and employment records, board minutes, grant contracts, beneficiary due diligence files, source of funds evidence, accounting system, tax invoices, IT equipment and data backup. Quantified risk: 35-45% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the municipal tax office or district court registry during the first fiscal year for a newly formed charitable endowment entity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 288 to 316 (formation of stock corporations), Article 295 (notarization and subscription), Article 301 (payment into bank), Article 303 (remedies for unpaid share capital), Article 312 (first meeting of incorporators), and Article 313 (election of directors); read together with the Act on the Establishment and Operation of Public Interest Corporations and the Act on the Regulation of Fund-raising and Donations for the charitable endowment and grant-making activities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registration Office of the Seoul Central District Court and the Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea, with territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered office; for non-Seoul entities, the district court registration office having jurisdiction over the principal office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Stock Company (Chusik Hoesa), accompanied by the Articles of Incorporation; filed through the Internet Registration Office (Electronic Registration System) of the Korean Supreme Court.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Korean Commercial Act. A Chusik Hoesa may be incorporated with zero statutory minimum paid-up capital; however, the aggregate subscription price of the issued shares must be fully paid into a Korean bank before registration, evidenced by a bank deposit certificate. No blocked escrow account is required. If public donations are solicited, donated funds must be segregated in a designated donation account and may be used only for the approved philanthropic or scientific grant purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF KR_CHUSIKHOESA. WHEREAS the Corporation was formed as a stock company (Chusik Hoesa) under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea on __________, with registration number __________, and its registered office is located at __________, and its Articles of Incorporation have been duly approved and registered by the competent Court Registration Office; WHEREAS the Corporation has issued __________ fully paid ordinary shares in the aggregate amount of KRW __________, all subscriptions having been paid into a domestic bank in accordance with Articles 295 and 301 of the Commercial Act; WHEREAS the Corporation has been established to manage charitable and scientific endowment assets, to distribute grants, and to carry out the activities described in its object clause; WHEREAS all directors are lawfully present and constitute a quorum under the Articles; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED: 1. The share

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, with electronic administration and filing through the HomeTax System (hometax.go.kr), and business registration administered through the NTS district tax offices and the Korea Trade Facilitation System for associated export registrations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Chusik Hoesa in South Korea, the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) is the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) issued by the competent district tax office under the Framework Act on National Taxes. The non-resident incorporator must appoint a local tax representative if it has no domestic place of business, but for a domestic Chusik Hoesa the entity itself is registered as a domestic corporation. Procedure: (1) file articles of incorporation with the Commercial Registration Authority; (2) register the corporation with the court registry; (3) file an application for business registration with the National Tax Service through HomeTax or by visiting the district tax office, using the prescribed application form for corporate business registration and attaching the certificate of incorporation, corporate registration certificate, lease agreement or proof of domestic place of business, and identification documents of the representative and directors; (4) the NTS reviews and issues the BRN, which is the combined corporate TIN and VAT ID. For a foreign non-resident entity that does not form a domestic Chusik Hoesa but has Korean-source income subject to tax or a VAT registration obligation, the NTS additionally assigns a foreign-invested company or non-resident TIN through the same business registration process; where no domestic business place exists, a non-resident tax representative registration is made and the foreign entity receives a non-resident registration number. The Chusik Hoesa must also register for social security and local tax (local income tax) identification through the integrated local tax system, but the primary TIN remains the NTS BRN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for general entity classification. The Chusik Hoesa is a domestic corporation taxable at the entity level under the Corporate Income Tax Act and is not eligible for a check-the-box partnership classification. However, if the Chusik Hoesa qualifies as a non-profit corporation or public-interest corporation under Article 24 of the Corporate Income Tax Act and is engaged in philanthropic endowment management and scientific grants, it may elect or apply for tax-exempt status on a restricted scope of income, and may separately apply for approval as a public-interest corporation under the Act on Establishment and Management of Public-Interest Corporations. Such elections are statutory status elections, not hybrid mismatch elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea, administered by the National Tax Service.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold: any person supplying taxable goods or services in the course of business, including corporations, is mandatorily required to register for VAT, regardless of revenue amount. A simplified VAT registration threshold of KRW 80 million annual turnover applies to small businesses for simplified taxation, but a Chusik Hoesa engaged in endowment management, grants, and digital content operations is generally not eligible for simplified taxation if it performs taxable activities. For non-resident electronic service suppliers and cross-border digital services, a special simplified registration is required when annual Korean-source e-service supplies exceed KRW 10 million (approximately USD 7,500).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Korea mandates full electronic tax invoice (e-tax invoice) issuance and real-time transmission to the NTS through HomeTax for all VAT-registered businesses. Since December 31, 2012, all tax invoices must be issued electronically through the HomeTax electronic invoicing system or approved third-party e-invoicing APIs integrated with HomeTax. Each e-tax invoice is automatically assigned a digital approval number by the NTS in real time, and the supply transaction is immediately recorded in the national anti-fraud database. A cash receipt must be issued for all sales to non-business final consumers, with mandatory issuance through the cash receipt system for any transaction occurring in the course of business. For cross-border services and exports, the export invoice or electronic export tax invoice must be filed with supporting customs export declarations in the UNI-PASS system. Failure to issue or transmit e-tax invoices triggers 2% penalties on the supply value and additional administrative penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Value-Added Tax Act of Korea, a zero-rating (0% VAT) applies to (1) the supply of exported goods, defined as goods delivered to a foreign country or to a free trade zone; (2) the supply of services rendered to non-residents or services rendered in a foreign country, including intermediate services related to exported goods; and (3) digital services or other electronically supplied services provided to non-resident consumers if the place of supply is treated as outside Korea. For the Chusik Hoesa, zero-rating is available for the export of qualifying strategic content, digital assets, research outputs, and certain offshore services, provided the actual benefit occurs outside Korea and the recipient is a non-resident. Grant distributions themselves are not a taxable supply and are outside the VAT system; endowment management services rendered to foreign charitable counterparties can qualify as zero-rated export services if the service is performed or consumed outside Korea and documented as a cross-border supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Electronically submitted Bill of Entry / Export Declaration) accepted by Korea Customs Service in UNI-PASS
Commercial invoice in English or Korean evidencing the exported goods/services and the buyer
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing the physical movement of goods out of Korea
Foreign exchange remittance record: Inward Remittance Certificate or Foreign Exchange Transaction Confirmation from a Korean bank licensed for foreign exchange business
SWIFT/FX payment receipt confirming actual receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Export contract, purchase order, or service agreement with the foreign counterparty
Electronic tax invoice issued as a zero-rated export invoice through HomeTax
Certificate of service performance or utilization evidence proving the digital service or grant-related service was used outside Korea
Recipient certification of non-resident status (e.g., foreign corporate registration extract or passport of foreign individual), where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to strict post-export audit by the National Tax Service and Korea Customs Service. The exporter must substantiate zero-rating with the full statutory documentation bundle above, and foreign exchange proceeds must be repatriated and received in Korea within 180 days of the export date unless an extension is approved by the Commissioner of the NTS or the Bank of Korea under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. If the inward remittance is not received within the 180-day deadline or documented evidence is incomplete, the NTS shall deny zero-rating and assess 10% VAT retroactively, impose daily interest under the Framework Act on National Taxes, and deny input VAT credits related to the export. For fraudulent export claims, fictitious export invoices, or false lost-in-transit certificates, penalty taxes of up to 40% of the unpaid VAT are imposed, together with the additional 10% VAT amount. Criminal referral to the prosecution can result in tax evasion charges punishable by imprisonment of up to 2 years or fines up to 3 times the evaded tax. The NTS and Korea Customs Service also jointly verify customs declarations, shipping manifests, foreign exchange receipts, and invoices through centralized cross-agency data matching; any mismatch triggers a full tax audit and immediate clawback of zero-rated refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (the central bank) together with the Foreign Exchange Policy Division of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the statutory foreign exchange administration authority
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains a free-floating Korean won with full current-account convertibility under Article 9 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Capital-account transactions are generally liberalized but remain subject to declaration and in certain situations prior approval. For a private charitable foundation receiving offshore endowment, the KRW is freely convertible into USD, EUR, and other major currencies within designated foreign exchange banks. Inward donations are treated as current transfers provided the underlying charitable purpose is documented. There is no surrender requirement for endowment or investment income. However, every inward remittance above the statutory threshold must be reported through the receiving foreign exchange bank, and the foundation must produce the donation agreement, the donor identification package, and evidence of the public-interest purpose. Outbound grant distributions to foreign beneficiaries are lawful current transfers, but the Korean bank must verify the ultimate beneficiary, verify the grant contract, screen sanctioned parties, and record the appropriate foreign exchange purpose code. The Bank of Korea may ask for the foundation's internal control and treasury investment policy to ensure that the structure is not a disguised for-profit treasury or a conduit for money laundering. In practice, convertibility is constrained by strict FATF-aligned Know Your Customer and Foreign Transactions Reporting obligations rather than by direct quantitative limits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable to a non-exporting private charitable foundation. Under the general Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act framework, export proceeds must be collected through a designated foreign exchange bank within 180 days from the date of the export declaration, or within the contractually approved payment term where an extension has been recorded. There is no mandatory conversion ratio to KRW; the exporter may hold foreign currency in a Foreign Currency Account, convert freely, or net against approved foreign liabilities. Overdue export collections require a written explanation to the foreign exchange bank and may be referred to the Bank of Korea for a compliance review.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Very Low and legally insufficient as a primary banking rail. A foreign digital EMI or electronic money institution is not a licensed bank under the Korean Banking Act and cannot lawfully propose KRW current accounts or direct foreign exchange conversion services to a Korean legal entity. A Korean-licensed fintech can only act as a payment facilitator or supplementary payout rail when operating through a designated commercial bank settlement account. For a statutory private charitable foundation requiring capital escrow, grant distribution, and strict AML traceability, the mandatory primary account must be held at a domestic tier-1 commercial bank; the EMI may only be used as an optional downstream disbursement channel for grantees where permitted by the underlying grant contract and the governing bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch presence is normally required for the statutory representative or a registered attorney-in-fact during corporate account onboarding. Most Korean tier-1 banks do not permit fully remote corporate opening for foreign-controlled entities. A remote consular proxy opening is accepted only exceptionally when the bank receives an apostilled and notarized power of attorney, passport copies, corporate registry excerpts, an English/Korean board resolution, and a completed financial crime risk assessment. In such cases, one Korea-based signatory, legal counsel, or an authorised bank officer must still complete an in-person identity verification step before the account is activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign charitable founder and donors are not physically available in Korea; the ultimate source of the endowment is opaque.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled and notarized founder/donor identity documents, donor bank reference letters, audited financial statements, wealth-sourcing documents, donation agreements, National Tax Service donation receipts, and an independent legal opinion confirming the charitable character of the foundation under the Korean Commercial Act and the Charitable Foundation supervision regime.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The foundation's treasury purpose may be mischaracterized as a private asset-management shell because the entity type is Chusik Hoesa despite its charitable scope.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of private charitable foundation registration, MOEF/regulator approval letter for ISIC 6430 endowment management, certified articles of incorporation, board minutes approving the treasury and grant-making policy, a clearly restricted investment policy, and a programme budget segregating philanthropic grants from operational expenses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border grant outflows could be perceived as disguised payments to related parties or shell beneficiaries for money laundering purposes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete grantee KYC files for each beneficiary, ultimate beneficial ownership registry extracts, sanctions screening results, executed grant agreements with a transparent charitable purpose, project budgets, and audited trail of grant milestones, which must be separately retained for each remittance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inward foreign donations may be viewed as unusual capital injections inconsistent with the entity's not-for-profit status.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-verified donor remittance declarations, original bank credits through SWIFT MT103, foreign exchange acquisition reports filed with the receiving bank, donation certificates issued to donors, and an external auditor's capital verification report confirming the funds were recorded in the restricted endowment account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Donors execute an irrevocable donation agreement and remit through SWIFT MT103 to the foundation's designated KRW or USD account at a tier-1 Korean bank. The receiving bank completes the Foreign Exchange Acquisition Declaration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, records the appropriate purpose code for donations and grants, and screens the donor against Korean, UN, EU, OFAC, and FSS sanction lists. Amounts above the statutory reporting threshold require a Foreign Exchange Transaction Report to the Bank of Korea through the bank's compliance team. Following credit, an external Korean auditor verifies the capital inflow, ties it to the donation agreement, and issues a capital verification statement covering the restricted charitable endowment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For grant distributions, the foundation sends a board-approved grant instruction and the bank executes a SWIFT MT103 using the foreign exchange purpose code for charitable transfers. For expenditure related to scientific equipment or contracted research procurement, settlement may occur through Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700), Documentary Collections, or Sight Drafts against shipping and service evidence. Domestic KRW disbursements are cleared through Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute (KFTC) and the Bank of Korea Won Wire. All outgoing payments must retain grant agreements, beneficiary KYC, procurement invoices, delivery verification, and compliance approval records in the foundation's treasury audit file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: KRW/USD deliverable forward contracts up to 12 months covering documented future grant disbursements and endowment investment repatriations
FX swaps through a designated Korean bank for temporary conversion of USD endowment into KRW for operating liquidity, with full underlying exposure documentation

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permitted only with a licensed Korean bank where the underlying exposure is proven and cannot be used for speculative proprietary trading, with the transaction recorded under the foundation's approved treasury mandate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular General Meeting of Shareholders and Approval of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company Secretary / National Tax Service (for tax purposes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the regular general meeting must be held and financial statements approved by March 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the regular general meeting within the statutory period constitutes a violation of the Korean Commercial Act, subject to a maximum administrative fine of KRW 20,000,000 (approximately USD 15,000) for the company, and individual penalties for directors; unresolved financial statement approval may trigger tax penalties and a court-ordered audit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (including charitable endowment income and donation disclosures)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service, Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 of the immediately following tax year for calendar-year taxpayers; a one-month extension is available by filing an application, extending the deadline to April 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file: 20% of the tax payable as a non-filing penalty; under-reporting: 20% penalty on the under-reported amount; fraudulent under-reporting: 40% penalty; interest accrues monthly at 0.66% of the deficient tax. Administrative strike-off of the corporate registration and suspension of the charitable foundation license may follow prolonged delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax office (Si/Gun/Gu) with jurisdiction over the registered head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months of the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, filed by April 30 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A non-filing or under-reporting penalty of 20% of the local income tax due, plus interest at 0.66% per month; enforcement proceedings and asset seizure may follow, and the local surtax delinquency is a critical impediment to annual clearance certificates required for government grants.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of Public Interest / Charitable Endowment Activities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent supervisory ministry (typically the Ministry of Economy and Finance for private charitable foundations) or the court of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of the fiscal year-end (by March 31 for calendar-year entities), unless a special extension is granted by the supervising authority.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual report may result in revocation of the charitable foundation license, administrative fines up to KRW 10,000,000 (approximately USD 7,500), and forced dissolution by the competent court; sustained non-filing is a statutory ground for strike-off from the charitable entity register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report Submission (where audit thresholds are met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (as an attachment to the corporate income tax return) and the regular general meeting for shareholder approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The audit report must be completed and presented to the regular general meeting before the March 31 financial statement approval date; the audited financial statements must be attached to the corporate income tax return filed by March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If a statutory audit is required and not performed, the company is prohibited from paying dividends, directors are subject to administrative fines, and the company may be designated for a tax investigation; the auditor may also be subject to sanction for failure to report irregularities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (Korean External Audit Act), an independent certified public accountant audit is mandatory for a Chusik Hoesa if any of the following criteria apply: (1) total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.0 million) as of the fiscal year-end; (2) total revenue exceeds KRW 70 billion (approximately USD 52.5 million); (3) for non-listed stock companies, outstanding debt greater than KRW 7 billion; or (4) the company falls within a specially designated public interest category under Article 2 of the External Audit Act. Additionally, for charitable foundations incorporated as stock corporations under the Civil Act, an audit by a licensed CPA is statutorily required when total assets at the fiscal year-end exceed KRW 1 billion (approximately USD 750,000) or when the aggregate amount of donations and grants received during the fiscal year exceeds KRW 500 million (approximately USD 375,000). A fund manager handling extensive endowment assets under the Endowment Management for Philanthropic and Scientific Grants designation is also subject to annual audit under the Ministry of Strategy and Finance guidelines if a minimum of KRW 3 billion in foreign grant funding is managed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean IFRS (K-IFRS) for entities required to meet international accounting standards; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) for private stock corporations; for charitable endowment activities, the Non-Profit Corporation Accounting Standards (established by the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the National Tax Service) apply with respect to restricted funds, grant liabilities, and endowment principal. Financial statements must be prepared in Korean won and comply with the Accounting Standards for Non-Statutory Non-Profit Organizations when the entity is a charitable public interest corporation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a public annual UBO confirmation registry for ordinary stock corporations; however, the annual corporate income tax return requires a schedule of significant shareholders stating all holders of 5% or more of issued shares and a beneficial ownership declaration for all assets managed in a fiduciary capacity. For charitable foundations, the competent ministry (Ministry of Economy and Finance) imposes an annual confirmation of the foundation's actual controlling contributor(s) and direct beneficiaries, filed simultaneously with the annual activity report by March 31. Any transfer of shares or alteration of the controlling beneficial owner of a charitable Chusik Hoesa must be reported to the competent supervisory authority within 30 days of the registration of the share transfer in the Register of Members, and the foundation must update the corporate register and secure ministerial approval before any new beneficial owner can exercise voting rights in the endowment committee.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges, Mortgages and Security Interests
Minute Book (shareholder resolutions and board resolutions)
Register of Board of Director Meetings
Register of Issued and Outstanding Shares with Beneficial Ownership Annotations

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 1,200 per year for a qualified corporate secretarial agency providing a registered address, legal correspondence handling, and annual filing coordination in Seoul or a provincial major city
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 per year for an independent audit of a mid-sized private Chusik Hoesa holding charitable endowment assets, with the fee varying based on asset complexity and number of grant transactions; for a simpler foundation, the lower quartile is approximately USD 5,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive national corporate income tax: 10% on taxable income up to KRW 200,000,000; 20% on KRW 200,000,001 to KRW 20,000,000,000; 22% on KRW 20,000,000,001 to KRW 300,000,000,000; 24% on taxable income above KRW 300,000,000,000. A 10% local income tax surcharge is imposed on the national corporate tax, producing aggregate headline exposure ranging from 11.0% to 26.4% depending on the taxable income bracket.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday applies to a private charitable endowment corporation. A Charitable Foundation recognized as a public-interest legal entity under the Corporate Tax Act may obtain exemption for non-profit-making income if the articles of incorporation require the income to be used directly for the public-interest purpose. Donation expenses paid for the performance of the public-purpose service are deductible as special expenses under CTA Article 24. Other preferential mechanisms include domestic intercorporate dividend exemptions, foreign tax credits, and investment or R&D tax credits under the Tax Incentive Limitation Law. None of these incentives is automatic; each requires an annual compliance election and documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return Form No. 30 together with supporting schedules, identified as the Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Calculation Statement, submitted via the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal at www.hometax.go.kr or filed directly at the competent regional tax office of the corporation's principal place of business.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. The final corporate tax return is mandatory once per fiscal year. Temporary caretaker filings are required on a semi-annual basis: an interim corporate tax payment for the first six months is due by 31 August, and the second-half interim payment is due by 28 February of the following year. Quarterly filing applies only to VAT obligations, which are outside the corporate income tax return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The final corporate income tax return must be filed within three months after the end of the fiscal year. For a corporation whose fiscal year ends on 31 December, the statutory filing deadline is 31 March of the following calendar year. If that day falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday, the deadline is extended to the next business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number, corporate legal name, representative director, filing agent identification, tax period start and end dates, type of business code, and corporate class checkbox (foreign-invested enterprise, public-interest corporation, small or medium enterprise status, or other).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder is not named in this section unless the Korean corporation is a branch or the foreign shareholder appears as representative director, guarantor, or nominated officer. When applicable, the foreign shareholder's name, country of residence, and foreign registration number must be entered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from the endowment, including fund management fees, investment gains, grant administration income, and any service revenue from scientific or charitable grant programs, recognized under K-IFRS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately disclose all foreign-source revenue and all Korean-source revenue attributed to the domestic corporation. Do not net foreign withholding taxes against the gross amount in this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income excluded from taxable gross income, including public-interest income exempt under CTA Article 12, dividends qualifying for exclusion under CTA Article 18-3, and refunded donations previously designated for public-interest purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule describing each exempt item and the statutory basis. A foreign parent company or grantor must provide supporting documentation that the exemption does not contravene the beneficial ownership clause of the applicable tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book-tax reconciliation worksheet computing adjusted taxable income after reversing statutory reserves, non-deductible provisions, entertainment expense limitations, and domestic dividend receipt exclusions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident is required to include all income attributable to a Korean permanent establishment under the force of attraction principle. Head office expenses are deductible only if evidenced by an internal accounting allocation actually borne by the Korean entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of unused tax losses from prior fiscal years against current adjusted income, subject to the legal carryforward period and to the annual limitation imposed for large taxpayers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean legal entity may offset only its own losses. Losses of a foreign parent or sister entity are non-deductible. A branch shall follow the subdivision of assets and liabilities statement to prevent the use of non-Korean losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Positive taxable amount after deduction of net operating loss carryforward and all other statutory adjustments. This is the amount to which the progressive national corporate tax brackets are applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that all profit components economically attributable to Korean management activities are included. Allocation to a low-tax foreign office is presumed invalid without evidence of actual personnel and decision functions in Korea.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed national corporate tax, after applying foreign tax credits, tax credits for employment increases, investment credits, disaster credits, and any reduction or exemption granted under the Tax Incentive Limitation Law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credit is available only when the Korean domestic corporation pays foreign income tax on Korean-source income taxed abroad in violation of treaty allocation. The credit amount must be supported by Form for Overseas Tax Payment and an apostilled Foreign Tax Certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Line item reconciling withheld taxes on dividends, interest, royalty, and other services received; also records interim corporate tax prepayments for the first half and second half of the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent deriving dividends from the Korean company is not reported on this schedule unless the Korean company is acting as a withholding agent for the non-resident shareholder. In such cases, report the statutory withholding rate, treaty-reduced rate, and attached Certificate of Residence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the final return by the statutory deadline results in an unfaithful-return penalty equal to 10% of the underpaid tax; fraudulent omission or concealment raises the penalty to 40%; aggravated tax evasion cases carry a 60% penalty. The local income tax surcharge follows the national penalty. Late payment interest accrues daily at approximately 0.022% to 0.025% from the original due date to the date of full settlement. Persistent non-filing authorizes the tax office to assess the tax by estimation, seize bank accounts and trade receivables, and impose criminal liability for deliberate non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The statutory withholding tax rate on dividend distributions by a Korean domestic corporation to a non-resident shareholder is 20% national income tax, plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on the national tax, producing an aggregate statutory rate of 22%. Treaty relief may reduce the national tax without eliminating the local surcharge in most Korean DTAs, so the aggregate effective rate after treaty relief is usually the applicable treaty rate multiplied by 110%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Korean paying corporation or its remittance agent must submit Form 24-6, 'Application for Reduction or Exemption of Non-Resident Taxation', to the National Tax Service prior to remittance. The application must be accompanied by the Certificate of Residence issued by the shareholder's home-country competent authority, a beneficial ownership declaration, evidence of corporate substance, and, for the reduced direct-dividend rate, proof of the minimum ownership percentage and holding period. Filing is available through HomeTax or at the regional tax office with jurisdiction over the Korean source payer. Without valid presentation of the TRC and Form 24-6 at payment time, the statutory rate is withheld and remedies are limited to a subsequent tax refund claim within the statutory prescription period, subject to additional audit scrutiny.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by a Korean resident to a non-resident for the use of intellectual property in Korea are subject to a 20% national withholding tax and an additional 2% local surcharge, producing an aggregate 22% statutory rate. Interest paid by a Korean corporation on borrowings, bonds, or loans from a non-resident lender is likewise subject to a 20% national withholding tax plus a 2% local surcharge, aggregating 22%. Treaty restrictions usually cap the national withholding rate at 10% or 15% for interest and at rates between 5% and 15% for royalties. To invoke a treaty cap, the beneficial owner must submit Form 24-6 with a valid TRC and documentary evidence that the royalties or interest are indeed connected to the Korean use and are not hidden equity distributions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Korean Chusik Hoesa must prepare and attach a Local File when its international transactions with related parties during the fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 5,000,000,000. A Master File is mandatorily required when the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue reaches KRW 100,000,000,000 and the Korean entity's aggregate international related-party transaction amount exceeds KRW 10,000,000,000. The annual 'List of International Related-Party Transactions' schedule must be submitted with the corporate tax return even when transaction amounts fall below these thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea applies a substance-over-form doctrine through the National Tax Basic Law, the force of attraction principle, the beneficial ownership test, and controlled foreign corporation rules. There is no standalone ESR filing regime comparable to the UAE or BVI economic substance regulations. Instead, a private charitable foundation acting as an endowment vehicle must demonstrate sufficient Korean commercial substance through board meetings, managerial control, physical office presence, actual grant decision-making, and qualified local staff. Absent such substance, the Korean tax authorities may disregard the legal form, treat the foundation as a sham, deny treaty benefits, or require consolidation into a foreign parent's Korean taxable presence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting endowment investment income, falsifying charitable grant invoices, classifying personal or commercial expenses of shareholders as foundation donations, or maintaining dual sets of books to understate the Korean corporate tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty tax of 40% to 60% of the evaded national corporate tax, with an additional 10% local income tax surcharge and daily overdue interest. Criminal conviction under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act carries imprisonment of up to three years or a fine equal to up to five times the amount of tax evaded. The court may also prohibit the offender from operating, suspend corporate licences, and confiscate diverted assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Executive and non-executive directors who directed or acquiesced in concealment may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes to the extent of the corporation's inability to settle. Personal exposure includes travel bans, asset freezing orders, restitution to the charitable purpose, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the Korean foundation as a letter-box entity with foreign nominee directors, managed from a tax-favored holding company, generating artificial grants and service fees to a related Cayman or Hong Kong entity solely to achieve a lower dividend withholding or interest withholding rate under a treaty not otherwise available to the ultimate beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of the treaty claim and requiring full 22% withholding; addition of a 40% unfaithful-return penalty and a 20% aggravated assessment under the Framework Act on International Tax Adjustment; reclassification of grants as constructive dividends; possible administrative taxation on deemed Korean source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute the artificial chain may be held personally liable for the unreported tax as constructive trustees of the foundation's assets. Criminal sanctions include imprisonment for up to three years and fines; civil recovery measures allow tax authorities to pierce the corporate veil when the foundation exists only as a sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the public charitable foundation to receive donor funds from unidentified foreign persons, mixing donation flows with commercial endowment income, and then wiring grants to shell charities in high-risk jurisdictions without AML risk assessment or disclosure to the Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sanctions under the Proceeds of Crime Act and the Financial Transaction Reports Act, including fines of up to KRW 500,000,000, confiscation of the proceeds of the violation, suspension from acting as a grant-making institution, and revocation of registration as a charitable or non-profit entity. Individuals involved face imprisonment of up to five years for money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for AML and charity compliance may be disqualified from serving as trustees, personally fined, and ordered to return misappropriated donor funds. Repeated or large-scale money laundering triggers asset seizure, international travel bans, extradition exposure, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Documentation and Transfer Pricing Mismatch
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a corporate tax return without the mandatory Local File, Master File, or annual related-party transaction schedule; recording management fees or royalty payments to the foreign parent without signed contracts, evidence of actual service performance, or consistent TP benchmarking under CUP or TNMM; and understating revenue through self-produced invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Rejection of the deducted management fees or royalties, application of an upward arm's-length adjustment, imposition of the 20% unfaithful-return penalty on the recomputed tax, accrual of daily unpaid interest, and correction of foreign tax credit claims. The National Tax Service may also order civil surcharges of 10% of the disallowed amount and criminal fine exposure of up to KRW 50,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who signs a false tax return and in doing so knowingly transmits false information to the tax office is personally liable for the resulting penalty where the corporation becomes insolvent. The director faces disqualification, travel bans, personal restitution for the lost tax revenue, and a term of imprisonment of up to one year for filing false declarations.
